transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. I'm Dr. [Your Name]. What brings you in today?

Hi, Dr. [Your Name]. I came in because... well, for a while now, I've been convinced that certain people in the arts and finance circles here in Cincinnati are quietly tracking which clients I meet with. It's like they're sending me little signals through invitations, or the topics at panels, or even who sits near me at events. And... even when I try to tell myself it could just be a coincidence, I just can't really let it go. It's been bothering me.
When you say people are sending you signals through invitations, panel topics, or who sits near you at events, do you feel they are doing this on purpose to communicate something to you personally?

Yeah, I do. It feels very intentional. Like I mentioned, it really seems like they know exactly which clients I'm meeting with. So, if I take on someone new, suddenly the panel discussion at the next networking event is about their exact industry, or the person sitting next to me brings up something way too specific to be random. 

I try to look at it logically—I mean, I look at data and trends for a living—and I tell myself it’s just a coincidence. But it just keeps happening. I can't shake the feeling that they're doing it on purpose, just to let me know they're watching my moves.
Have you noticed anything else unusual, like hearing voices, seeing things others don’t, or having thoughts that feel like they’re being put into your mind?

No, no I haven't noticed anything like that. I don't hear voices or see things that aren't there. And my thoughts... they definitely feel like my own. It's really just the patterns I'm noticing with the people at these events. But nothing like what you're asking about, no.
Have you ever felt that your thoughts or actions are being controlled by external forces, or that you're receiving special messages that others aren't meant to understand?

No, I don't feel like anyone is controlling what I do or think. I'm definitely the one in control of my own actions. 

And as for special messages... well, I mean, I talked about the signals at the networking events. But it's not like I'm getting secret messages from the universe or something mystical that no one else can understand. It's really just those specific people in my professional circle doing things to show me they know my business. So, no, nothing is controlling me, and I'm not getting any special messages like that.
Have you ever had any beliefs or ideas that you know others might find strange or unfounded, even if they weren't related to the events or people you've been describing?

No, not really. I mean, outside of what I've been telling you about the networking events and the people in my industry, I don't have any other ideas like that. I'm pretty grounded in reality, you know? My work is all about numbers and practical planning. So, no, I don't have any strange beliefs or anything else going on. It's just... just the stuff with my clients and those events.
How much distress or disruption has this belief caused in your daily life—like at work, in relationships, or in social situations?

Well, I'm still working, so it hasn't completely stopped me. But... yeah, it has caused some disruption. My practice has actually gotten a bit smaller lately. I just find myself missing follow-ups, and I've been avoiding some of the public panels I normally attend. It's just... it's been harder to keep up the same level of client contact that I used to manage. So it's definitely taking a toll on the business side of things.
Outside of your professional events and client interactions, have you ever had any other experiences where you felt others were sending you intentional signals or messages?

No, not really. Like I said, it's pretty much just tied to my work and those networking events. When I'm at the grocery store or just out running errands, I don't feel like anyone is paying attention to me or sending me signals. It's really just isolated to my professional circle and the people I interact with for my business. Outside of that, everything feels pretty normal.

Even though you said you try to tell yourself these signals are just coincidences, do you ever fully believe that, or do you always come back to feeling certain that the signals are real and intentional?

Honestly, no, I don't think I ever fully believe it's just a coincidence. I always come back to feeling like it's real. That's actually the main reason I came in to see someone. 

For a while now, I've just been convinced that certain people in the arts and finance circles here in Cincinnati are quietly tracking which clients I meet with. It feels like they're sending me these little signals through the invitations I get, the specific panel topics they choose, or even who ends up sitting near me at events. I really do try to be logical and tell myself it could just be a coincidence, but... I just can't really let it go. I always come back to being certain that it's intentional.
Has there ever been a time when you doubted your belief about these signals being sent to you, or has it remained completely certain for you the entire time?

Yeah, I mean, like I was just saying... I do try to doubt it. I tell myself it might just be a coincidence. But the doubt never really sticks. 

I always end up right back where I started—completely convinced that these people in the Cincinnati arts and finance circles are tracking my client meetings. The signals they send... the invitations, the specific panel topics, who they sit me next to... it just feels too real. So, to answer your question, no, I haven't really been able to doubt it for long. I just can't let it go, which is exactly why I decided to finally come in and talk to someone.
Have you ever been presented with evidence or arguments that contradict your belief about these signals being sent to you, and if so, how did you respond to that?

I haven't really shared this with anyone else, so I haven't had someone sit down and actually try to argue with me about it. But I do try to look at the evidence myself. Like, I'll look at a seating chart or an event schedule and try to find a boring, logical reason for it. 

But... well, like I was saying earlier, it doesn't really matter what the logical argument is. Even when I try to present myself with evidence that it could just be a coincidence, I just can't really let it go. I'm still completely convinced that those people in the arts and finance circles here in Cincinnati are quietly tracking which clients I meet with. No matter how I try to rationalize it, those little signals—the specific panel topics, the invites, who sits next to me—they just feel too deliberate to ignore.

So even when you try to convince yourself that these signals might not be real, you still feel completely certain they are happening. Would you say your belief in this never changes, even for a moment?

Yeah, I'd say that's accurate. It really doesn't change. I mean, I might have a brief second where I think, okay, maybe this is just random. But it's fleeting. It always comes right back to that same certainty. 

Like I mentioned, that's the whole reason I'm here. I just can't shake this conviction that these folks in the Cincinnati arts and finance scene are keeping tabs on my client meetings. And those signals—the invites, the panel topics, the seating arrangements—they just feel too specific. Even when I try my hardest to chalk it up to coincidence, the feeling never actually goes away. I just can't let it go.

Have you ever encountered a situation where the evidence was completely clear and undeniable that the signal you thought you received was actually just a normal, unrelated occurrence? If so, did that change your belief at all, even briefly?

Not really, no. I haven't had a situation where there was some... smoking gun, I guess, that proved it was all just a normal occurrence. 

I mean, like I keep coming back to, that's exactly why I came in to see someone. I've just been convinced for a while now that these specific people in the Cincinnati arts and finance circles are quietly tracking which clients I meet with. They keep sending me these little signals through the invitations, the panel topics, even who sits near me at these events. And even when I try to find that clear evidence myself, or I tell myself it could just be a coincidence... I just can't really let it go. 

So, no, I haven't had an experience that undeniably proved it was just a normal thing and changed my mind. The feeling is always just there.
Would you say your belief that these people are sending you signals is something you know for certain, like other facts in your life, or does it feel more like a suspicion that won’t go away?

I'd say it's something I know for certain. It's not just a passing suspicion. Like I've been saying, that's the whole reason I'm here. I'm just absolutely convinced that these people in the arts and finance circles here in Cincinnati are tracking my client meetings. The signals they send—the invitations, the panel topics, the seating arrangements—they're real to me. Even when I try to tell myself it's just a coincidence, I can't let it go. It feels as real and certain as anything else in my life.
